title: Typo Hunt
body:
Goal: this program should draw a flag on a pole, but it has 4 typos. Find them and fix them.

  1. Open starter.py in Thonny and press Run (F5).
  2. Python stops at the first bug and shows a red message in the Shell. Read it like a detective:
    • the line number tells you where to look,
    • the last line says what Python did not understand.
  3. Fix that one typo. Press Run again. Repeat until there is no red text.

Clues: Python is picky about capital letters, spelling, and names. Compare each line with a line that already works.

Done looks like: no red error, the Shell says Typo hunt: fixed!, and the turtle draws a pole with a flag at the top (4 lines).

Extra: write down each bug you fixed and the line number. Which one was the sneakiest?

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Press Run and read the red message in the Shell. It names a line number, so go to that line. The last line of the message tells you what Python did not understand.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: Python cares about capital letters and exact spelling. Compare the broken line with a similar line that works, letter by letter. Fix only one typo at a time, then press Run again to find the next one.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Each typo is small, like one wrong letter or one capital letter that should be small. Look for the line number in the red message, then check each word in that line, such as t.____(90). Keep going until the red text is gone. Remember, there are 4 typos in all.

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# Typo Hunt!
# This program should draw a flag on a pole.
# It has 4 typos. Run it, read the red message, fix ONE typo, run again.

import turtle

t = turtle.Turtle()
t.shape("turtle")
t.color("#0072B2")
t.pensize(4)

Print("Typo hunt: fixed!")

# The pole goes up
t.left(90)
t.forwad(150)

# The flag
t.right(90)
t.forward(80)
t.Right(90)
t.forward(50)
t.right(90)
t.forward(80)

turtle.Done()
